product_backlog.title: To-Do List Management MVP
product_backlog.description: Core features for managing to-do lists and tasks for a single user.
As a user, I want to create a new to-do list with a name so that I can organize my tasks.
product_backlog.title: Create a New To-Do List
product_backlog.value_hypothesis: Users can successfully initialize and view new lists, establishing the core container for tasks.
acceptance_criteria: Given the user is on the home page, When they enter a name for a new list and click create, Then a new to-do list is created and displayed in the application.
product_backlog.user_story: As a user, I want to create a new to-do list with a name so that I can organize my tasks.

product_backlog.value_hypothesis: Users have visibility into all their created lists from the main interface.
product_backlog.description: As a user, I want to see all my lists so that I can choose which one to view or manage.
acceptance_criteria: Given the user has created a to-do list, When they view the main page or lists view, Then all created to-do lists are listed with their names.
product_backlog.title: View All To-Do Lists

product_backlog.value_hypothesis: Users can populate lists with actionable tasks.
acceptance_criteria: Given the user is viewing a specific to-do list, When they enter a short text description and add a task, Then the task appears within that list.
product_backlog.title: Add Task to a List
product_backlog.description: As a user, I want to add a task to a list with a short text description so that I can track what needs to be done.

acceptance_criteria: Given the user is viewing a list with tasks, When they view the task items, Then completed tasks are visually distinguished (e.g., struck-through or grayed out) from incomplete ones.
product_backlog.description: As a user, I want to see all tasks within a list with completed tasks visually distinguished from incomplete ones so that I can easily review progress.
product_backlog.title: View Tasks and Visual Distinction
product_backlog.value_hypothesis: Users get clear visual feedback on task completion status.

product_backlog.title: Mark Task Complete or Incomplete
product_backlog.description: As a user, I want to mark a task as complete or incomplete so that I can track my progress.
product_backlog.value_hypothesis: Users can update task status dynamically.
acceptance_criteria: Given the user has a task in a list, When they mark it as complete or incomplete, Then its status toggles accordingly and updates visually.

product_backlog.value_hypothesis: Users can prune unwanted tasks from lists.
product_backlog.title: Delete a Task
acceptance_criteria: Given the user has a task in a list, When they delete the task, Then it is removed from the list.
product_backlog.description: As a user, I want to delete a task so that I can remove items I no longer need.

acceptance_criteria: Given the user has created a list, When they choose to delete the entire list, Then the list and all its contained tasks are removed from the application.
product_backlog.description: As a user, I want to delete an entire list (and its tasks) so that I can remove obsolete lists.
product_backlog.value_hypothesis: Users can clean up entire lists and associated data.
product_backlog.title: Delete Entire List

# Fixed Evaluation Scenario: To-Do List Web App

> **Do not edit this file to "make the eval easier" or to match whatever the team

This is the fixed input fed verbatim to the agent team as the product vision for
every automated team-performance evaluation run (see `RELEASE.md` "Team performance
evaluation" and `agents/scrum_team/scripts/run_eval.py`). It is intentionally small
enough to be fully deliverable within a 5-sprint, small-budget run, while still
requiring real design decisions (state persistence, list vs. item modeling,
basic UI) that differentiate a good team performance from a mediocre one.

## Product Vision

Build a simple to-do list web application. A single user should be able to:

1. Create a new to-do list with a name.
2. Add a task to a list, with a short text description.
3. Mark a task as complete or incomplete.
4. Delete a task.
5. Delete an entire list (and its tasks).
6. See all their lists and, within a list, all its tasks, with completed tasks
   visually distinguished from incomplete ones.

## Constraints (deliberately narrow, to keep this deliverable in 5 sprints)

- **Single user, no authentication.** Do not build login/accounts — out of scope.
- **No persistence requirement beyond the current session/process is assumed** unless
  the team's own design calls for it — persistence approach (in-memory, file, or a
  simple embedded DB) is a legitimate design decision for the team to make and
  justify, not a hidden requirement.
- **A working web UI is required** — the deliverable is something a person could
  open in a browser and actually use, not just a backend API with no way to
  interact with it.
- **No specific language/framework is mandated.** The team should choose something
  it can deliver completely and correctly within budget, and should say why.

## Explicitly out of scope (do not let these creep in)

- Multiple users, sharing, or permissions.
- Due dates, reminders, priorities, tags, or sub-tasks.
- Mobile app, offline support, or real-time sync.
- Any deployment/hosting beyond running locally.

## What "done" looks like after 5 sprints

A person can clone the repo, follow the README, run the app, and actually create a
list, add a few tasks, mark one complete, delete one, and delete a list — end to
end, without reading any code first.

Do not ask me anything else during this sprint - make reasonable decisions yourself and note them as assumptions in the sprint report.

# Fixed Evaluation Scenario: To-Do List Web App

> **Do not edit this file to "make the eval easier" or to match whatever the team

This is the fixed input fed verbatim to the agent team as the product vision for
every automated team-performance evaluation run (see `RELEASE.md` "Team performance
evaluation" and `agents/scrum_team/scripts/run_eval.py`). It is intentionally small
enough to be fully deliverable within a 5-sprint, small-budget run, while still
requiring real design decisions (state persistence, list vs. item modeling,
basic UI) that differentiate a good team performance from a mediocre one.

## Product Vision

Build a simple to-do list web application. A single user should be able to:

1. Create a new to-do list with a name.
2. Add a task to a list, with a short text description.
3. Mark a task as complete or incomplete.
4. Delete a task.
5. Delete an entire list (and its tasks).
6. See all their lists and, within a list, all its tasks, with completed tasks
   visually distinguished from incomplete ones.

## Constraints (deliberately narrow, to keep this deliverable in 5 sprints)

- **Single user, no authentication.** Do not build login/accounts — out of scope.
- **No persistence requirement beyond the current session/process is assumed** unless
  the team's own design calls for it — persistence approach (in-memory, file, or a
  simple embedded DB) is a legitimate design decision for the team to make and
  justify, not a hidden requirement.
- **A working web UI is required** — the deliverable is something a person could
  open in a browser and actually use, not just a backend API with no way to
  interact with it.
- **No specific language/framework is mandated.** The team should choose something
  it can deliver completely and correctly within budget, and should say why.

## Explicitly out of scope (do not let these creep in)

- Multiple users, sharing, or permissions.
- Due dates, reminders, priorities, tags, or sub-tasks.
- Mobile app, offline support, or real-time sync.
- Any deployment/hosting beyond running locally.

## What "done" looks like after 5 sprints

A person can clone the repo, follow the README, run the app, and actually create a
list, add a few tasks, mark one complete, delete one, and delete a list — end to
end, without reading any code first.

Use this living roadmap to plan releases and track user stories across states. It doubles as a lightweight task board and a release planning tool.

## How to use
- Story IDs should match files in `specs/stories/` (e.g., `ST-001` corresponds to `specs/stories/ST-001-some-title.md`).
- Move story references between states as work progresses.
- Keep titles short; full details live in the story file.
- For each planned version, list goals and the set of stories targeted for that release.
- When a release is cut, freeze the section by adding the actual tag (e.g., `v0.1.0`) and dates.

Legend
- `[ST-###] Title` → a user story reference and its short title
- Checkbox states: `- [ ]` To Do, `- [~]` In Progress (use `- [~]` to signal WIP), `- [R]` In Review, `- [x]` Done

Tip: If you prefer standard checkboxes only, use the Kanban tables below and keep raw lists unchecked.

## Release checklist (for when cutting a release)
- [ ] All included stories are in `Done` and meet Definition of Done
- [ ] Docs updated (stories, PRD/SRS, ADRs as needed)
- [ ] Version/tag created (e.g., `v0.1.0`) and changelog drafted
- [ ] Known issues captured and follow-ups added to backlog
